sources.title: Rutter et al. (2001): NAD cofactors and clock DNA binding
sources.scope: Purified protein system; does not establish a human circadian disorder or ADHD etiology.

sources.title: van Andel et al. (2021): circadian timing in adults with ADHD and delayed sleep phase
sources.scope: 51 adults with both ADHD and delayed sleep phase; short follow-up and selected population. Not generalizable to all ADHD.

sources.title: Verlaet et al. (2019): oxidative and immune biomarkers in ADHD
sources.scope: Case-control comparison: erythrocyte GSH was higher, not lower, in the ADHD group; several other differences lost significance after multiple-testing correction. Peripheral markers do not establish brain status or causation.

sources.title: Surman et al. (2019): adjunct L-methylfolate trial
sources.scope: 44 adults; no broad benefit over placebo as an adjunct to methylphenidate. Does not support a general folate explanation for ADHD.

sources.title: Demontis et al. (2023): ADHD genetic architecture
sources.scope: ADHD has a distributed genetic architecture. Risk associations do not identify an individual biochemical bottleneck.

sources.title: NIMH: ADHD overview
sources.scope: ADHD symptoms and possible causes; the map is not a diagnostic assessment.

nodes.label: Folate cycle
nodes.summary: Reduced folates carry one-carbon units. This overview combines several cytosolic and mitochondrial reactions; it is not a single flux.

nodes.label: Methionine / SAM cycle
nodes.summary: Remethylation and methionine metabolism connect homocysteine to the methyl donor S-adenosylmethionine (SAM).

nodes.label: Transsulfuration
nodes.summary: The human pathway converts homocysteine through cystathionine toward cysteine, a precursor for glutathione.

nodes.label: Glutathione synthesis
nodes.summary: Glutamate, cysteine and glycine supply glutathione synthesis. Synthesis and recycling are separate processes.

nodes.label: Pentose phosphate
nodes.summary: The oxidative branch generates NADPH. The non-oxidative branch interconverts sugars; the branches are not interchangeable.

nodes.label: NADPH / NADP+
nodes.summary: A reducing-cofactor pool, not a pathway. Compartment-specific redox balance cannot be inferred from a symptom.

nodes.label: Glutathione recycling
nodes.summary: Glutathione reductase uses NADPH to reduce GSSG back to GSH. This reaction does not measure overall oxidative stress.

nodes.label: Catecholamine methylation
nodes.summary: COMT uses SAM in dopamine metabolism. This is one component of catecholamine handling, not a model of synaptic dopamine levels.

nodes.label: Circadian clock
nodes.summary: CLOCK/BMAL and PER/CRY feedback contribute to cellular timing. Cell-autonomous clocks and organism-level sleep timing are distinct.

nodes.label: Melatonin synthesis
nodes.summary: Serotonin is converted to melatonin; the methylation step uses SAM. Synthesis, circadian phase and sleep behavior are not equivalent.

nodes.label: Circadian phase / sleep
nodes.summary: A timing phenotype rather than a metabolic reaction. Delayed circadian phase was studied in a selected group of adults with ADHD.

nodes.label: ADHD research context
nodes.summary: A heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition, not the output of one metabolic pathway. Symptom overlap and research associations do not establish etiology.

edges.label: 5-methyl-THF / remethylation
edges.note: Folate-dependent remethylation is a biochemical connection; direction of net change depends on context, including B12.

edges.label: homocysteine branch
edges.note: A substrate connection, not a prediction that more methylation means more glutathione.

edges.label: cysteine supply
edges.note: Cysteine can supply GSH synthesis; other substrates and regulation still matter.

edges.label: NADPH generation
edges.note: Oxidative pentose phosphate reactions generate cytosolic NADPH.

edges.label: one-carbon redox reactions
edges.note: Folate reactions exchange reducing equivalents; direction and compartment differ by enzyme.

edges.label: reducing equivalents
edges.note: NADPH is used by glutathione reductase. This is not the only use or source of NADPH.

edges.label: GSSG → GSH
edges.note: Recycling replenishes reduced glutathione; the map groups the GSH pool with synthesis for navigation.

edges.label: SAM methyl donor
edges.note: SAM is a COMT substrate; this connection does not predict neuronal dopamine concentration.

edges.label: SAM methyl donor
edges.note: SAM supplies the methylation step in melatonin biosynthesis; it is not a sleep-phase prediction.

edges.label: redox-sensitive DNA binding
edges.note: Purified-system result for NAD cofactors. Extrapolation to symptoms or ADHD remains a hypothesis.

edges.label: cell clock ↔ whole-person timing
edges.note: Cross-scale context only: cellular clock activity is not a direct measurement of sleep phase.

edges.label: DLMO timing marker
edges.note: Dim-light melatonin onset was used as a phase marker; melatonin quantity alone does not specify phase.

edges.label: selected-population trial
edges.note: Trial in adults with both ADHD and delayed sleep phase; this does not make circadian delay the cause of ADHD.

edges.label: redox biomarker research
edges.note: The case-control study found higher erythrocyte GSH; it did not measure a GSR deficit. This research association neither supports a universal low-glutathione account nor establishes causation.

edges.label: adjunct trial: no broad benefit
edges.note: A null adjunct-treatment trial is a constraint on extrapolation, not proof that folate can never matter.

hypotheses.title: Circadian timing contribution
hypotheses.summary: Assume a delayed phase is contributing to the observed difficulties. Inspect timing independently of the ADHD label.
hypotheses.limits: The trial population had both ADHD and delayed sleep phase. Inattention alone does not establish circadian delay.
questions: What is the sleep schedule on free days versus required days?
Does the timing precede the attention difficulties?
Which observations would favor a sleep explanation over this one?

hypotheses.title: Folate / remethylation bottleneck
hypotheses.summary: Assume a constraint on folate-dependent one-carbon transfer. Trace links to SAM and sulfur metabolism without assuming downstream increases or decreases.
hypotheses.limits: Low folate or elevated homocysteine is not specific for a particular enzyme. A small ADHD adjunct trial found no broad benefit; no MTHFR variant-to-symptom inference is implemented.
questions: Is the hypothesis based on a measured finding or on symptoms alone?
What alternative nutritional, physiological or measurement explanations remain?
What evidence would contradict a one-carbon explanation?

hypotheses.title: Glutathione recycling constraint
hypotheses.summary: Assume reduced NADPH-dependent GSH recycling. Inspect cofactor supply and synthesis separately.
hypotheses.limits: An altered peripheral redox assay does not identify GSR dysfunction or brain redox status. Case-control evidence cannot establish ADHD causation.
questions: Which analyte, compartment, timing and assay were actually measured?
Could production, consumption or sample handling explain the result?
What would distinguish impaired synthesis from impaired recycling?

hypotheses.title: Altered catecholamine methylation
hypotheses.summary: Assume a change in COMT-mediated methylation and inspect its SAM connection. The direction of neural or behavioral effects is left unspecified.
hypotheses.limits: A biochemical substrate dependency does not establish a dopamine deficit, ADHD cause, or effect of a common COMT variant.
questions: What evidence supports an enzyme-level change?
Which other synthesis, release, uptake and degradation processes are missing?
Could the same symptoms arise without this mechanism?
